findings.explanation: The flagged line `stmt = select(User).where(User.username == user2.username)` is a SQLModel/SQLAlchemy ORM query. SQLModel's `select()` with `.where()` compiles to a parameterized SQL statement with bound values — no string concatenation or interpolation is involved. Additionally, the value `user2.username` is a hardcoded test string 'testuser2' defined in the test itself (line 88 of the diff), not user-controlled input. The same pattern is used in production code (crud.py line 14: `select(User).where(User.username == username)`), confirming this is the standard safe ORM idiom in this codebase.

The PR changes the DELETE /api_key/{api_key_id} endpoint to pass current_user.id into delete_api_key(db, api_key_id, current_user.id), clearly intending to enforce ownership. However, the only delete_api_key implementation I could observe (crud.py:44-49) has the signature delete_api_key(session, api_key_id) and performs NO ownership check — it fetches the ApiKey by id and deletes it unconditionally. The PR diff does not include a corresponding change to crud.py, and grep confirmed only one definition of delete_api_key exists in the repo (crud.py:44). If the service-layer function is not updated to accept and enforce the user_id parameter, the endpoint will either fail at runtime (TypeError) or, if a 3-arg version is added without an ownership filter, remain vulnerable to IDOR: any authenticated user could delete another user's API key by supplying its UUID. The sibling GET endpoint (api_key.py:17-28) scopes by user_id via get_api_keys(db, user_id), confirming the intended per-user ownership model, but the delete path lacks that scoping in the observed code. Because I could not confirm whether a 3-arg delete_api_key with an ownership check exists elsewhere (budget exhausted), the flaw is plausible but not definitively confirmed.

evidence.content:
async def delete_api_key(session: AsyncSession, api_key_id: UUID) -> None:
    api_key = await session.get(ApiKey, api_key_id)
    if api_key is None:
        msg = "API Key not found"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    await session.delete(api_key)
For more information, see [API keys and authentication](https://docs.langflow.org/api-keys-and-authentication).

findings.suggested_fix: Update delete_api_key in crud.py to accept a user_id parameter and scope the query to the owner, e.g. `async def delete_api_key(session, api_key_id, user_id): api_key = await session.get(ApiKey, api_key_id); if api_key is None or api_key.user_id != user_id: raise ValueError('API Key not found'); await session.delete(api_key)`. Return 404 (not 403) when the key does not belong to the requester to avoid leaking the existence of other users' keys. Ensure the endpoint passes current_user.id and that no other code path calls the unscoped variant.
